jobs.title: Housing Navigator
jobs.description:
The position of Housing Navigator reports directly to an assigned Program Coordinator at a U.S.VETS site. The Housing Navigator is responsible for assisting veterans and their families and other persons served in navigating the housing process up to obtaining permanent housing, often while coordinating with multiple agencies and support types including the HUD-VASH housing voucher. The Housing Navigator manages and motivates the clients through housing search, application, and lease negotiation. The Housing Navigator directly supports the HUD-VASH Social Workers/Case Management team with veteran housing support and maintains regular and extensive contact with the veteran’s care team.

Specific duties may be established via a Housing Navigation program agreement between Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) grantees and HUD-VASH which may include additional elements not listed here.

FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt

Responsibilities

Act as a liaison between U.S.VETS programs and the Veterans Administration (VA) and other partnering agencies, managing a caseload of clients needing support with their housing search
Work closely with HUD-VASH partners, attending case conferencing and collaborating with assigned VA Social Workers on veteran clients and their needs
Maintain case file of documents necessary for clients’ application to housing opportunities
Consider client needs for housing search of available housing inventory and consulting with landlords and property management offices to search inventory
Develops and maintains positive relationships with landlords, property managers and residential real estate specialists
Compiles client information, rental market information, and housing trends to provide data for reports and to guide decisions
Provides limited and short-term case management to clients and their families with the purpose of securing and maintaining permanent housing
Engage clients at various levels of the housing process
Meet with clients in person at least every other week. Conduct virtual meetings (phone call, online meeting) during off-weeks when not seeing a clients in person
Conduct outreach to engage clients to participate in housing navigation services with additional efforts for any non-participatory clients. Due diligence to find and engage clients includes calling collateral contacts, visiting the site or area they reside, visiting clinics or other service environments they frequent, bringing the client’s name to the local by-name list case conferencing and other coordinated entry system meetings to brainstorm how to find and engage the client
Assess for housing choice, tenant-screening barriers, and strengths
Assist clients to locate housing, view units (including transport clients to units in company vehicles or securing transportation), collect documents owners require, apply for units, and mitigate or overcome any tenant-screening barriers
Submit required housing documents to various agencies to advance housing process
Conduct landlord engagement and outreach in coordination with multiple agencies
Assist clients with’ accessing allowable incentives (landlord & clients), move-in costs, sign the lease and all moving logistics
Provide up to 1 month of housing stability case management to veteran client enrolled in HUD-VASH, who have moved to permanent housing, before transitioning fully to a HUDVASH point of contact for clinical care and ongoing/continued case management
Provide housing stability case management to clients as required for other programs
Support clients’’ basic needs (non-clinical care) and provide case management including setting up a housing stability plan and coordinating referrals for supportive services not offered by U.S.VETS
Provide linkages to VA and community-based services to pursue healthcare, public benefits, utility discounts, legal services, employment programs and other services to assist with housing search and stability
Perform other duties as assigned

Additional Program-Specific Duties

For Housing Navigators working with SSVF:

Housing Navigators assigned to the Supportive Services for Veteran Families Program (SSVF) shall gain and maintain knowledge of the SSVF program to include eligible activity, client eligibility, goals, and regulations and are also to become knowledgeable of all U.S.VETS programs and share resources and care coordination efforts.
Perform other SSVF or U.S.VETS duties as assigned.

For Housing Navigators working with a Housing Navigation Program such as a County or other local program:

Housing Navigators may report to a Housing Navigation Coordinator
Gain and maintain knowledge of the assigned program to include eligible activity, client eligibility and enrollment, client discharge or transition planning, program goals and regulations and are also to become knowledgeable of all U.S.VETS programs for client referrals and intake, sharing resources, collaborating outreach efforts, and coordinating care
Conduct street and community outreach to specific areas assigned to engage clients and community partners
Conduct case management as required by the program
Conduct intakes for veterans and their families into U.S.VETS programs
Participate in community meetings and trainings
Maintain case records, outreach data, housing inventory and placement data, and other pertinent information in internal and external systems
Perform other Housing Navigation program or U.S.VETS duties as assigned

Qualifications

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in social services/social work or a closely related field that would support the duties and qualifications of the position required
For Housing Navigators working with SSVF programs, a Bachelor’s degree is required
For Housing Navigators working with a Housing Navigation Program such as a County or other local program, a Bachelor’s degree is required or may be substituted equivalent experience if permitted by funding source and site management

Experience working with low income and/or homeless populations, preferably those in low-income subsidized housing arrangements and/or supportive housing programs
Proficient typing and computer skills, including Microsoft Office 365 (Outlook/Word/Excel)
Ability and willingness to work flexible hours to accommodate participants which may include evenings and/or weekends
Experience working in diverse settings with people across all socio-economic spectrums and a wide variety of roles - staff, residents, local agencies, contractors, lenders, etcetera
Professionalism: high level of integrity and strong ethical values show capacity to maintain highest standards of confidentiality with all records, including organizational and individual information
Strong oral/written communication and listening skills
Self-motivated, well-organized, and accountable for work time, deadlines, and agency resources
Quality control: demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness, monitors own work to ensure quality, and applies feedback to improve performance
Access to reliable personal transportation required, including a Valid driver’s license, must meet company insurance requirements and complete a provided driver training course

We are proud to be an AAHA Accredited practice, signifying our commitment to the highest standards of veterinary care. This dedication is reflected in the trust we have built within our community, evidenced by our excellent 4.8-star Google rating. We are seeking collaborative and compassionate veterinary professionals to join our dedicated team and contribute to a culture where you can immediately feel welcome and supported. We understand that to provide excellent care, we must first support our teammates. While you will be working specifically at Roadside Veterinary Clinic, you join a larger network dedicated to ensuring you can do your best work. This network prioritizes career growth for all teammates, whether that means mentorship for new doctors, tuition support for those looking to become a credentialed technician, or specialized internal training opportunities. We provide the resources and education you need to succeed in your professional journey. Our commitment to delivering high-quality small animal care means equipping our hospital with the tools necessary for modern veterinary practice. Furthermore, through our network affiliations, our veterinarians have direct access to internal specialty consultations and continuing education, ensuring that even complex cases benefit from a wide breadth of expertise. This structure allows us to consistently offer comprehensive medical, surgical, and preventative care while empowering you to expand your clinical skill set. Highland, Michigan, offers a beautiful blend of peaceful community living and accessible outdoor recreation. Located in Oakland County, you will find yourself surrounded by state parks, lakes, and rolling landscapes, making it an ideal location if you appreciate a slower pace and opportunities for hiking, boating, or simply enjoying nature. This locale maintains a strong small-town feel, yet you are still within easy driving distance of the greater metro Detroit area when you desire city amenities. It is a welcoming place where you can easily find balance between your dedicated career and a quality personal life.

Your Impact as a Patient Care Coordinator

As a Patient Care Coordinator, you will be the central point of contact for our clients, guiding them through their entire visit from check-in to check-out. You will serve as a vital link between the client and the medical team, capturing medical notes, creating treatment plans, and coordinating all aspects of patient care to ensure a seamless and supportive experience.

Your Impact Will Include

Setting the Stage for a Great Visit: You'll contact clients before their appointments to set expectations, answer questions, and ensure they are prepared for their visit.
Acting as a Medical Scribe: You will be in the exam room to capture real-time medical information from the veterinarian, ensuring all records are accurate and up-to-date.
Creating Treatment Plans: You'll create, present, and clearly explain treatment plans to clients in accordance with the veterinarian's directions.
Coordinating Seamless Care: You will collaborate with the technical team to ensure the veterinarian's treatment plan is completed efficiently and handle all in-room check-outs, including payments and scheduling follow-ups.
Educating Clients: You'll clearly explain discharge instructions, ensure prescription fulfillment, and address any client inquiries.
Following Up with Care: You will conduct post-visit follow-ups to check on the well-being of pets and communicate any test results.

What You'll Bring To The Team

A high school diploma or equivalent.
A genuine love for animals and a passion for delivering exceptional client service.
A friendly, personable, and empathetic demeanor.
Proficient in active listening, with strong computer literacy and typing skills for accurate medical transcription.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Knowledge of (or eagerness to learn) veterinary medical terminology is preferred.

How You're Supported

As part of the Mission Pet Health family, you get the stability of a local practice backed by the comprehensive benefits and resources of a larger network. The focus is on investing in you, so you can focus on what you love.

Competitive Compensation

A competitive hourly rate based on your experience, plus a comprehensive benefits package.

Total Wellbeing

Comprehensive coverage including Health, Dental, and Vision insurance, plus access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

Financial Health

Commitment to Growth

The Power of a Network

Join a nationwide community of over 20,000 veterinary professionals who share a passion for collaboration and career growth.

Valuable Perks

Enjoy paid time off, discounted veterinary care for your own pets, and free 24/7 access to doctors through Teladoc.

About Mission Pet Health

Mission Pet Health was founded by veterinarians on the belief that local practices thrive with clinical autonomy, collaboration, and medical excellence. The organization provides world-class support to its 850+ hospital teams on a hyper-local basis so they can focus on what matters most: the medicine, their patients, and their team culture. The Program Manager is a full-time position serving as a primary public representative of The Business Center Miami (TBCM), a program of the Greater North Miami Chamber of Commerce with the primary function of promoting and supporting women entrepreneurship.

TBCM is in part funded by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) as a Women’s Business Center (WBC), providing federally supported resources, counseling, and training to women entrepreneurs and small business owners across Miami-Dade and Monroe Counties.

Major Duties & Responsibilities

Implement and manage all aspects of The Business Center Miami (TBCM) program.
Collaborate with staff to plan and organize program logistics including scheduling presenters, recruiting participants, negotiating contracts, and managing communications.
Promote TBCM and related events through online, email, and direct marketing channels.
Develop and administer post-program evaluations to assess impact and outcomes.
Build and maintain positive working relationships with internal staff and external stakeholders.
Ensure all program activities operate within organizational policies and procedures, as well as SBA/WBC grant compliance requirements and federal program guidelines.
Anticipate, understand, and respond to the needs of internal and external clients to meet or exceed expectations.
Work cooperatively with colleagues to set goals, resolve problems, and make decisions that enhance organizational effectiveness.
Monitor program metrics and outcomes regularly per the program evaluation framework and SBA WBC reporting protocols.
Positively influence others to achieve results aligned with organizational goals.
Serve as a liaison with SBA district office staff, WBC national network partners, and other federally funded resource partners (SCORE, SBDC, etc.).
Coordinate and conduct one-on-one business counseling sessions or connect clients to appropriate certified advisors.
Develop and deliver or coordinate workshops, training, and educational programming tailored to women entrepreneurs at various stages of business development.
Assist the President or Designee with additional organizational programs and activities as assigned.

Metric Reporting

Analyze program revenues and expenses on an ongoing basis.
Identify strategies to improve program performance and sustainability.
Support achievement of organizational goals and contribute ideas for revenue development.
Prepare grant report metrics detailing program outcomes, including SBA-required WBC annual and semi-annual performance reports (EDMIS data entry, client tracking, training hours, counseling hours, jobs created/retained, capital accessed).
Maintain accurate and up-to-date client records in the SBA’s EDMIS system and any internal CRM or database.
Track and report on program outputs and outcomes including number of clients served, businesses started, revenue generated, and loans/capital obtained by clients.
Collaborate with the Executive Director or Designee on member outreach initiatives to support TBCM growth.

Administrative Operations

Assist with training and retention of interns and volunteers.
Maintain ongoing TBCM communications: answering and returning phone calls, attending workshops, scheduling presenters, responding to online inquiries, emailing participants, and conducting regular participant check-ins.
Support planning of the TBCM calendar and creation of project and event timelines.
Maintain confidentiality of client information in compliance with SBA and organizational privacy policies.
Assist in the development of the annual program workplan and budget in coordination with the Executive Director.
Coordinate with accounting/finance staff to track grant expenditures and ensure compliance with approved budgets.

Qualifications

Proven experience in business incubator services and/or program management, event planning, and communications.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and Google Workspace.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to think creatively and analytically.

jobs.title: NVIS Knowledge Management Program Manager
jobs.description:
NVIDIA Infrastructure Specialists (NVIS) deploy and support some of the world's most advanced AI infrastructure. Every deployment generates critical technical knowledge that enables faster execution, higher quality, and better customer outcomes. As NVIS continues to scale globally, knowledge management has become a strategic capability that directly impacts deployment velocity, operational excellence, and organizational learning. We are looking for a Knowledge Management Program Manager to guide and enhance the NVIS Knowledge Management initiative. This role is accountable for outlining the strategy, governance, operating model, and roadmap for knowledge management across NVIS.

You will direct the development of our Knowledge Management platform while encouraging organization-wide adoption, governance, content management powered by intelligent systems, and integration with NVIDIA's broader training and AI initiatives. You will ensure that technical knowledge is gathered, standardized, supervised, and readily available to accelerate AI Factory deployments worldwide! This role demands critical thinking and outstanding program leadership. It requires influencing others without authority. The role also needs skills to develop scalable programs that improve how an organization collects, shares, and employs knowledge.

What You'll Be Doing

Define and lead the long-term strategy, roadmap, and governance model for the NVIS Knowledge Management program.
Guide the creation of the Knowledge Base platform into the definitive reference for deployment, operational, and technical documentation across NVIS.
Establish program metrics and executive dashboards to measure adoption, content quality, knowledge coverage, operational health, and business impact.
Lead continuous improvement initiatives that simplify knowledge creation, improve discoverability, and increase organizational adoption.
Champion AI-enabled knowledge management, intelligent search capabilities, and automated content generation workflows.
Partner closely with NVIDIA Training & Education to align technical documentation, learning content, and enablement programs.
Drive organization-wide knowledge adoption through communications, organizational change, executive reporting, and engagement strategies.
Lead a small Knowledge Management team, providing direction, prioritization, and operational leadership while encouraging continuous improvement.
Represent NVIS within WWFO and influence enterprise-wide knowledge management practices and platform direction.

What We Need To See

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) in Knowledge Management, Communications, Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field
8+ years of program management, knowledge management, technical operations, or related experience leading complex multi-functional initiatives.
Consistent record in establishing or expanding enterprise Knowledge Management programs, including governance, content lifecycle oversight, and adoption strategies.
Demonstrated ability to define strategy, independently complete, and deliver measurable business outcomes with minimal direction.
Experience working with enterprise Knowledge Management or IT Service Management systems.
Experience developing executive-level metrics, dashboards, and program reporting.
Outstanding communication, executive presentation, and collaborator leadership skills.
Strong analytical outlook with the ability to use data to drive prioritization, decision making, and continuous improvement.
Ability to influence across organizations without direct authority.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience supporting AI infrastructure, data center operations, technical services, cloud infrastructure, or large-scale deployment organizations.
Experience implementing ServiceNow Knowledge Management solutions.
Experience integrating AI technologies into knowledge management workflows, including AI-assisted content generation, intelligent search, or retrieval-augmented systems.
Knowledge Management Professional (KMP) certification or similar formal knowledge management training.
Passion for redefining organizational knowledge into a strategic business capability that improves execution speed, quality, and operational excellence.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 168,000 USD - 258,750 USD for Level 4, and 200,000 USD - 322,000 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

new_jobs.description:
The position of Housing Navigator reports directly to an assigned Program Coordinator at a U.S.VETS site. The Housing Navigator is responsible for assisting veterans and their families and other persons served in navigating the housing process up to obtaining permanent housing, often while coordinating with multiple agencies and support types including the HUD-VASH housing voucher. The Housing Navigator manages and motivates the clients through housing search, application, and lease negotiation. The Housing Navigator directly supports the HUD-VASH Social Workers/Case Management team with veteran housing support and maintains regular and extensive contact with the veteran’s care team.

Specific duties may be established via a Housing Navigation program agreement between Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) grantees and HUD-VASH which may include additional elements not listed here.

FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt

Responsibilities

Act as a liaison between U.S.VETS programs and the Veterans Administration (VA) and other partnering agencies, managing a caseload of clients needing support with their housing search
Work closely with HUD-VASH partners, attending case conferencing and collaborating with assigned VA Social Workers on veteran clients and their needs
Maintain case file of documents necessary for clients’ application to housing opportunities
Consider client needs for housing search of available housing inventory and consulting with landlords and property management offices to search inventory
Develops and maintains positive relationships with landlords, property managers and residential real estate specialists
Compiles client information, rental market information, and housing trends to provide data for reports and to guide decisions
Provides limited and short-term case management to clients and their families with the purpose of securing and maintaining permanent housing
Engage clients at various levels of the housing process
Meet with clients in person at least every other week. Conduct virtual meetings (phone call, online meeting) during off-weeks when not seeing a clients in person
Conduct outreach to engage clients to participate in housing navigation services with additional efforts for any non-participatory clients. Due diligence to find and engage clients includes calling collateral contacts, visiting the site or area they reside, visiting clinics or other service environments they frequent, bringing the client’s name to the local by-name list case conferencing and other coordinated entry system meetings to brainstorm how to find and engage the client
Assess for housing choice, tenant-screening barriers, and strengths
Assist clients to locate housing, view units (including transport clients to units in company vehicles or securing transportation), collect documents owners require, apply for units, and mitigate or overcome any tenant-screening barriers
Submit required housing documents to various agencies to advance housing process
Conduct landlord engagement and outreach in coordination with multiple agencies
Assist clients with’ accessing allowable incentives (landlord & clients), move-in costs, sign the lease and all moving logistics
Provide up to 1 month of housing stability case management to veteran client enrolled in HUD-VASH, who have moved to permanent housing, before transitioning fully to a HUDVASH point of contact for clinical care and ongoing/continued case management
Provide housing stability case management to clients as required for other programs
Support clients’’ basic needs (non-clinical care) and provide case management including setting up a housing stability plan and coordinating referrals for supportive services not offered by U.S.VETS
Provide linkages to VA and community-based services to pursue healthcare, public benefits, utility discounts, legal services, employment programs and other services to assist with housing search and stability
Perform other duties as assigned

Additional Program-Specific Duties

For Housing Navigators working with SSVF:

Housing Navigators assigned to the Supportive Services for Veteran Families Program (SSVF) shall gain and maintain knowledge of the SSVF program to include eligible activity, client eligibility, goals, and regulations and are also to become knowledgeable of all U.S.VETS programs and share resources and care coordination efforts.
Perform other SSVF or U.S.VETS duties as assigned.

Housing Navigators may report to a Housing Navigation Coordinator
Gain and maintain knowledge of the assigned program to include eligible activity, client eligibility and enrollment, client discharge or transition planning, program goals and regulations and are also to become knowledgeable of all U.S.VETS programs for client referrals and intake, sharing resources, collaborating outreach efforts, and coordinating care
Conduct street and community outreach to specific areas assigned to engage clients and community partners
Conduct case management as required by the program
Conduct intakes for veterans and their families into U.S.VETS programs
Participate in community meetings and trainings
Maintain case records, outreach data, housing inventory and placement data, and other pertinent information in internal and external systems
Perform other Housing Navigation program or U.S.VETS duties as assigned

Qualifications

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in social services/social work or a closely related field that would support the duties and qualifications of the position required
For Housing Navigators working with SSVF programs, a Bachelor’s degree is required
For Housing Navigators working with a Housing Navigation Program such as a County or other local program, a Bachelor’s degree is required or may be substituted equivalent experience if permitted by funding source and site management

Experience working with low income and/or homeless populations, preferably those in low-income subsidized housing arrangements and/or supportive housing programs
Proficient typing and computer skills, including Microsoft Office 365 (Outlook/Word/Excel)
Ability and willingness to work flexible hours to accommodate participants which may include evenings and/or weekends
Experience working in diverse settings with people across all socio-economic spectrums and a wide variety of roles - staff, residents, local agencies, contractors, lenders, etcetera
Professionalism: high level of integrity and strong ethical values show capacity to maintain highest standards of confidentiality with all records, including organizational and individual information
Strong oral/written communication and listening skills
Self-motivated, well-organized, and accountable for work time, deadlines, and agency resources
Quality control: demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness, monitors own work to ensure quality, and applies feedback to improve performance
Access to reliable personal transportation required, including a Valid driver’s license, must meet company insurance requirements and complete a provided driver training course

NVIDIA Infrastructure Specialists (NVIS) deploy and support some of the world's most advanced AI infrastructure. Every deployment generates critical technical knowledge that enables faster execution, higher quality, and better customer outcomes. As NVIS continues to scale globally, knowledge management has become a strategic capability that directly impacts deployment velocity, operational excellence, and organizational learning. You will ensure that technical knowledge is gathered, standardized, supervised, and readily available to accelerate AI Factory deployments worldwide! This role demands critical thinking and outstanding program leadership. It requires influencing others without authority. The role also needs skills to develop scalable programs that improve how an organization collects, shares, and employs knowledge.

Define and lead the long-term strategy, roadmap, and governance model for the NVIS Knowledge Management program.
Guide the creation of the Knowledge Base platform into the definitive reference for deployment, operational, and technical documentation across NVIS.
Establish program metrics and executive dashboards to measure adoption, content quality, knowledge coverage, operational health, and business impact.
Lead continuous improvement initiatives that simplify knowledge creation, improve discoverability, and increase organizational adoption.
Champion AI-enabled knowledge management, intelligent search capabilities, and automated content generation workflows.
Partner closely with NVIDIA Training & Education to align technical documentation, learning content, and enablement programs.
Drive organization-wide knowledge adoption through communications, organizational change, executive reporting, and engagement strategies.
Lead a small Knowledge Management team, providing direction, prioritization, and operational leadership while encouraging continuous improvement.
Represent NVIS within WWFO and influence enterprise-wide knowledge management practices and platform direction.

What We Need To See

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) in Knowledge Management, Communications, Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field
8+ years of program management, knowledge management, technical operations, or related experience leading complex multi-functional initiatives.
Consistent record in establishing or expanding enterprise Knowledge Management programs, including governance, content lifecycle oversight, and adoption strategies.
Demonstrated ability to define strategy, independently complete, and deliver measurable business outcomes with minimal direction.
Experience working with enterprise Knowledge Management or IT Service Management systems.
Experience developing executive-level metrics, dashboards, and program reporting.
Outstanding communication, executive presentation, and collaborator leadership skills.
Strong analytical outlook with the ability to use data to drive prioritization, decision making, and continuous improvement.
Ability to influence across organizations without direct authority.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience supporting AI infrastructure, data center operations, technical services, cloud infrastructure, or large-scale deployment organizations.
Experience implementing ServiceNow Knowledge Management solutions.
Experience integrating AI technologies into knowledge management workflows, including AI-assisted content generation, intelligent search, or retrieval-augmented systems.
Knowledge Management Professional (KMP) certification or similar formal knowledge management training.
Passion for redefining organizational knowledge into a strategic business capability that improves execution speed, quality, and operational excellence.
